topic: What Azure AI Foundry is, why businesses adopt it, and what teams build with it
learn: Why the demo works and the product still does not ship
How one Foundry project holds the model, your data and the agent
What to evaluate and filter before a release, not after

faq.q: Why does an AI demo work but the product still not ship?
faq.a: A demo only has to answer once, well, on a curated question. Shipping requires evaluation against a real range of inputs, content filtering, and monitoring — the parts that don't show up in a five-minute demo but decide whether the product is safe and reliable in production.

faq.q: What does Azure AI Foundry actually bundle together?
faq.a: One project holding the model catalog, your own data, the agent built on top of it, evaluation tooling and safety guardrails — all under the same Azure identity and access controls, rather than stitching separate services together yourself.

title.main: From a model to a shipped AI product
title.sub: Azure AI Foundry is the platform Microsoft built for the part everyone underestimates — everything after the demo.

stages.title: The demo is easy. Shipping is not
stages.desc: Models, your data, evaluation, safety and monitoring — five separate tools, glued together by hand, each with its own SDK and its own outage.

stages.title: Azure AI Foundry is one platform
stages.desc: The catalog, the grounding, the agents, the evaluations and the guardrails live in a single Foundry project, sharing one connection string.

stages.title: Pick a model, not a lock-in
stages.desc: Frontier and open models — GPT, Llama, Mistral, DeepSeek — sit behind one endpoint shape, so changing model is a config change, not a rewrite.

stages.title: Ground it in your own data
stages.desc: Azure AI Search indexes your content with vector and keyword search together, so the model retrieves the right passages and cites them.

stages.title: Agents that actually do the work
stages.desc: Foundry Agent Service gives the model instructions, tools and a persistent thread — so it can call your APIs, not just answer in a chat window.

stages.title: Evaluate before your users do
stages.desc: Score groundedness, relevance and risk on every change before it ships, with content filters and automated red teaming built into the pipeline.

stages.title: Enterprise controls come built in
stages.desc: It deploys inside your own Entra ID tenant, VNet and compliance boundary, with distributed tracing on every request end to end.

stages.title: This is what teams ship with it
stages.desc: Support copilots, document processing, retail assistants, engineering agents — different teams, one platform and one bill underneath all of them.

end.title: Model to agent to production, in one place
end.sub: Azure AI Foundry: the catalog, your data, the agent, the evaluations and the guardrails — under one project and one set of Azure controls.

post.caption:
Most AI projects do not fail at the model. They fail at everything after it.

Azure AI Foundry is Microsoft’s answer to that gap: a model catalog you can swap without rewriting your app, grounding on your own data through Azure AI Search, the Foundry Agent Service for tools and actions, evaluations and content filters before release, and Entra ID, RBAC, private networking and tracing once it is live.

Same platform behind a support copilot, a document pipeline, a retail assistant or an engineering agent.

Which of these are you building first?
